identification.summary: Mandiant describes UNC5330 as a suspected China-nexus espionage actor [S1]. It chained CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2024-21887 to compromise Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances as early as February 2024, then used an Active Directory certificate-template abuse path to reach domain administrator and deployed the TONERJAM launcher and PHANTOMNET backdoor via WMI [S1]. Mandiant counted it as one of five China-nexus clusters among eight observed exploiting the Ivanti CVEs after the 10 January 2024 disclosure [S1][S3].
identification.firstObserved: Server infrastructure operational since 2021-12-06; Mandiant assesses with moderate confidence UNC5330 has operated through it since at least 2021 [S1]. Ivanti exploitation observed from February 2024 [S1].
identification.notes: UNC5330 is a Mandiant (Google) uncertain-attribution cluster; no Microsoft name, MITRE group or public overlap with a named APT is stated in the sources gathered [S1]. Do not merge facts from those clusters into this record.

attribution.confidence: Mandiant labels UNC5330 a 'suspected China-nexus espionage actor' and gives no overall attribution confidence level [S1]. The only stated confidence is moderate, for the assessment that the actor has operated through the GOST proxy server since at least 2021, based on SSH key reuse and temporal proximity [S1].
attribution.basis: Vendor reporting only: Mandiant observation of Ivanti exploitation, tooling and infrastructure overlap via SSH key reuse [S1]. No government attribution found.

objectives: Mandiant characterizes the activity as espionage [S1]. Specific collection objectives are not stated.

targeting.notes: Mandiant's post does not name victim organizations, sectors or geographies for UNC5330; it describes only compromised Ivanti Connect Secure appliances and Active Directory domains [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access by chaining Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2024-21887 [S1]. The actor used the appliance's ldap-ivanti LDAP bind account to create a domain computer object (testComputer$), requested a certificate from a vulnerable template granting enrollment to Domain Computers, obtained a certificate for a domain administrator, got a Kerberos TGT and performed DCSync [S1]. It used WMI ActiveScript event consumers to create and delete scheduled tasks for execution and to deploy tools; Mandiant noted the behavior matches a CrackMapExec version using DCE/RPC for WMI execution without SMB [S1]. TONERJAM is a launcher that decrypts and runs an encrypted shellcode payload (PHANTOMNET) and persists via Run key or COM object hijacking; PHANTOMNET is a modular backdoor using a custom TCP protocol with plugins mapped into memory [S1]. Infrastructure included a server used as a GOST proxy, with the default GOST certificate seen 2022-09-01 to 2024-01-01, and an attempted Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) download on 2024-02-03 from a compromised Ivanti device [S1].

diamond.adversary: Suspected China-nexus espionage cluster tracked by Mandiant as UNC5330; sponsor not identified [S1].
diamond.capability: Ivanti CVE-2024-21893/CVE-2024-21887 chain, AD certificate template abuse, DCSync, WMI event consumers, TONERJAM and PHANTOMNET, GOST and FRP tunneling [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: A server active since 2021-12-06 serving as GOST proxy and tool host, linked by SSH key reuse [S1].
diamond.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Connect Secure with integrated Active Directory; specific victims not named [S1].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing VPN appliances with LDAP bind accounts into AD, and permissive AD certificate templates enrolling Domain Computers [S1].

gaps: No named victims, sectors or regions for UNC5330 are published in the sources gathered [S1].
No sponsor or government attribution; overall attribution confidence not stated by Mandiant [S1].
No reporting after April 2024 found; a search for later UNC5330 activity returned nothing relevant.

Possible overlap with other Ivanti-exploiting clusters (UNC5221, UNC5266, UNC5291, UNC5325, UNC5337) is not stated for UNC5330; Mandiant noted one such suspected overlap only for UNC5337/UNC5221 [S1].
Press coverage (The Hacker News, Computing, Cybersecurity Dive) was seen only as search summaries, and the Hacker News page could not be fetched; Malpedia could not be fetched.
Network indicators were not tagged to UNC5330 in the Mandiant post [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the internet-facing VPN gateway and the AD domain it trusts, including LDAP bind service accounts and certificate templates [S1]. STEP 2: The actor reached domain admin from an edge appliance foothold, so a gateway compromise implies enterprise compromise [S1]. STEP 3: Template is edge-device exploit, then LDAP bind account abuse and certificate request, DCSync, then WMI-based deployment of TONERJAM/PHANTOMNET with proxy tunnels (GOST, FRP) [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued quiet espionage via VPN appliance exploitation (stated objectives are not public). MDCOA, an inference not in the sources, is use of the same chain against DoD-adjacent remote-access gateways after the next edge-device disclosure. Candidate indicators: unexpected computer objects such as testComputer$, certificate requests for administrator accounts from Domain Computers templates, ldap-ivanti account activity, WMI ActiveScript consumers and scheduled tasks writing .log files to C:\Windows\Temp, and the Mandiant PHANTOMNET YARA rule and file hashes [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track edge-VPN vulnerability disclosures and run vendor integrity checkers, as Mandiant recommends [S1]. (2) Authorities: remediation of AD certificate templates and service accounts sits with network owners; align requests through the supporting cyberspace operations chain. (3) Mission assurance: treat VPN gateways as single points of compromise for remote access and plan fallback access. (4) Coordination: share indicators from vendor reporting with DC3 and DIB partners; attribution is uncertain, so prioritize containment over naming [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC5330 is a suspected China-nexus espionage actor. UNC5330 has been observed chaining CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2024-21887 to compromise Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances as early as Feb. 2024. Post-compromise activity by UNC5330 includes deployment of PHANTOMNET and TONERJAM. UNC5330 has employed Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to perform reconnaissance, move laterally, manipulate registry entries, and establish persistence. Mandiant observed UNC5330 operating a server since Dec. 6, 2021, which the group used as a GOST proxy to help facilitate malicious tool deployment to endpoints. The default certificate for GOST proxy was observed from Sept. 1, 2022 through Jan. 1, 2024. UNC5330 also attempted to download Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) from this server on Feb. 3, 2024, from a compromised Ivanti Connect Secure device. Given the SSH key reuse in conjunction with the temporal proximity of these events, Mandiant assesses with moderate confidence UNC5330 has been operating through this server since at least 2021.
